author: Claude Opus 5.5 (engineering lead, cand-d author)
summary: Two-segment inline body (Family B), version 5, designed coupler-first. A long head segment (PA12 shell 33.8 x 25.4 x 24 mm) holds the cell, the coupler drive and the joint drive; a short tail segment (8.8 mm) holds the controller and carries the coupler stud. One vertical revolute joint (pin at mid-gap, 304 ears and plates, spur sector z58 driven by a 6 mm gearmotor) bends the chain in the table plane, +-15 deg working, outline contact at +-16.1 deg. The coupler is rigid and gendered: a one-piece 304 tail stud (Hirth-toothed flange, dia 4 pilot, two dia 3 lugs) enters the head cartridge: a one-piece 304 housing (front flange with a Hirth ring, lying on the front plate's outer face and screwed through it into two nut blocks, and a tube with axial lug slots) around a C95400 aluminium bronze cam sleeve whose two helical slots have a 20 deg capture stage and a 3 deg self-locking lock stage, on a PTFE thrust ring, retained by a 304 collar. A 6 mm gearmotor turns the sleeve to a 1.5 V stall, which seats the 36-tooth Hirth faces with 6.62 to 13.50 N typical preload (1.76 N guaranteed); axial tolerance is absorbed by sleeve travel inside the lock stage. Torsion and shear are carried by the Hirth teeth with zero lash. No spring, no SMA, no magnet. BLE only, no power transfer. Version 5 closes the items of retention-review-v4-r1 (Q93): a C95400 sleeve and PTFE-coated head teeth let the guaranteed lower-bound closing force roll and pitch units flat; a tighter pilot bounds yaw; the coupler motor is bonded into a 304 clip; a cell-voltage divider is declared.

assembly_access.statement: Each segment shell is one SLS part (bottom, two sides, end plate and inner wall) closed by a separate top lid that carries no declared load; all internal parts go in through the top. Head segment: the cell, coupler motor, joint motor, driver and hinge-ear legs are fitted from the top. The one-piece 304 housing (flange and tube) is pushed tube-first through the front plate window from outside until its flange lies on the plate's outer face; from inside, through the open top, the PTFE ring and the sleeve are slid onto the tube (stop pin engaged) and the retainer collar is pressed on; two countersunk M1.6 A2 screws go through the flange lobes and the plate into the two nut blocks held behind it. The coupler motor, bonded into its clip, is screwed to the floor from below. Tail segment: the stud flange is held on the end plate's outer face by two countersunk M1.6 screws driven from inside with a short L key through the open top into the flange's blind tapped holes, before the controller drops in; the lower hinge plate lies on the tail floor and is screwed from below. Hinge: the head ears' legs are screwed through the head inner wall from the gap side, the tail upper plate's leg through the tail inner wall from inside; the sector (part of the tail lower plate) is meshed with the joint pinion, then the pin is pressed through ears and plates from above. The harness passes the gap beside the pin. Not prototyped; the sequence is a paper statement.

coupler_sites.mount: head cartridge through the head front plate window; its 304 front flange (0.8 thick) lies on the plate's outer face, Hirth pitch plane at x 36.4, held by two countersunk M1.6 screws through the flange lobes and the plate into 304 nut blocks; axis (y, z) = (3.3, 1.0)
tail stud flange (r 6.3) on the tail end plate's outer face, held by two countersunk M1.6 A2 screws from inside into blind holes of the 304 flange; Hirth pitch plane at x -11.6; same axis (3.3, 1.0)

retention.mechanism: Holding principle: a self-locking cam (friction wedge). The two 304 lugs of the tail stud sit on the 3 deg lock stage of the C95400 aluminium bronze sleeve's helical slots. Axial lug load cannot turn the sleeve while flank friction exceeds tan 3 deg = 0.0524: steel on bronze dry 0.15 to 0.23 and machine oil 0.10 to 0.16 (Wikipedia Leadscrew, raw wikitext; aluminium bronze taken as a bronze) give 2.86x and 1.91x at the mean flank radius (2.08x and 1.39x at the inner end of the flank line); PTFE thrust friction adds holding torque that is not credited. Self-locking is friction-based and not absolute under vibration (same source). While the stage holds, the stud moves axially only by elastic deflection: an axial load 20 N above any preload opens the faces by at most 0.001 mm (loop stiffness lower bound 20 kN/mm), against a Hirth tooth height of 0.39 mm, so the two 36-tooth 90 deg Hirth faces (r 2.6 to 6.3) stay geometrically engaged at any preload and roll is bounded to 0.013 deg. Closing: the controller measures the cell (vsense divider) and drives the coupler motor at a 1.5 V PWM average to stall. Preload typical 6.62 to 13.50 N dry (7.87 to 17.03 oiled); guaranteed lower bound 1.76 N (datasheet rated load 3 mN m at 3 V and max start voltage 0.5 V give stall >= 1.2 (V - 0.5) mN m). Seating at the lower bound: the head teeth carry a bonded PTFE dry film (PTFE on steel mu 0.05 to 0.20, Engineering ToolBox), so the guaranteed draw rolls a unit flat (1.39 N needed to tip it about its far bottom edge, 1.27x) and pitches it flat (0.21 N, 8.3x). Yaw is bounded by the pilot (clearance 0.040 to 0.060, 0.69 deg); with that residual the seat stays inside the lock stage (stack +-0.0815 plus yaw +-0.059 = +-0.140 against +-0.20). The pilot's radial clearance (>= 0.020) exceeds the pilot-to-Hirth coaxiality (+-0.010 for two parts), so pilot and teeth do not fight. Tension (declared 1.223 N = 4 mu W, mu = 1): lugs on the self-locking stage; faces closed at typical F_p (5.41x) and at the lower bound (1.44x). Torsion (declared 7.77 mN m): Hirth teeth, zero lash, no face friction relied on; separation ratio 3.79 typical, 1.01 at the lower bound. With the teeth seated the lugs keep at least 2.29 deg of clearance to the 3.40 mm slots at the contact radius 3.5 (phase +-0.88 deg), so torsion goes only through the teeth and the lugs cannot slide along the flank. Shear (declared 0.306 N): Hirth teeth. Out-of-plane bending (declared 14.7 mN m): tipping 41.7 mN m (2.84x); beyond it the pilot couple (tilt <= 0.69 deg). In-plane bending (declared 14.5 mN m, the joint drive limit): tipping about y 5.87 (the slots remove 35 percent of the head ring) 38.8 mN m (2.68x); beyond it the lug pair on the self-locking stage. All declared loads at once: axial separating 3.27 N against typical F_p (2.02x); the residual clamp holds the combined bending (21.1 against 20.6 mN m). At the lower bound the faces may gap by micrometres under bending; gapping is not separation. Every load path is closed in machined metal or in one-piece SLS shells, and every screw joint to PA12 puts the thread in 304 (PA12 bearing only). Head mount: the 304 housing's front flange (disc r 7.0, lobes at +-z) lies on the front plate; two countersunk M1.6 screws through the lobes and the plate into nut blocks; worst 4.34 N per screw (fault), 1.53 MPa on PA12. Tail mount: two countersunk M1.6 screws from inside the end plate into blind holes of the 304 stud flange; worst 4.75 N per screw (fault), 0.94 MPa on the PA12 countersink. Plates as fixed-fixed strips (span 23 mm) under the worst screw load: head 15.5 MPa, tail 14.2 MPa against the Materialise PA12 tensile strength 48 MPa (3.1x, 3.4x). Contact stress: lug on bronze flank (2.65 mm line), Hertz p0 203 MPa at typical F_p_max, 244 MPa with all declared loads, 265 MPa oiled, fault 283, against a first-yield onset of about 369 MPa (1.67 x 221, rule of thumb). Axial stack: seat 3.518 to 3.681 at the IT9 / g6 corners inside the lock stage 3.40 to 3.80.

release.means: The head unit's own coupler motor turns the sleeve back to the open stop (304 stop pin dia 1 in the flange's rear face at r 5.3 in an arc groove of the sleeve face; worst stop load 7.3 N, shear 9.3 MPa, bronze bearing 14.6 MPa). Release is allowed only with the cell at 3.75 V or more (measured through the vsense divider); the motor then gets its maximum operating voltage 3.6 V (DRV8835 on-resistance 305 mOhm drops about 0.07 V). Release needs at most 27.8 mN m at the sleeve (typical F_p_max 13.50 N plus all declared axial loads, flank 0.23, thrust 0.20; 26.8 oiled) against 34.8 mN m (typical 3.6 V stall 10.8 mN m x 43/12 x 0.9): margin 1.25 dry, 1.30 oiled. Closing and release use the same motor, so with the voltage-linear model the margin is independent of motor-to-motor variation; with the datasheet start-voltage offset (up to 0.5 V) the ratio of release to closing torque rises. The capture stage's outer flank pushes the stud out 1.4 mm; the reaction goes into the 304 retainer collar. Release is a physical process under load and may be slow or blocked by loads beyond the declared ones, or when the cell is below 3.75 V (CPL-008). The tail unit cannot release this joint; each head releases its own joint.

alignment.description: Lateral: 45 deg chamfers on the pilot nose (0.3) and the flange's bore mouth (0.4, from the inner land recessed 0.25 below the pitch plane), leading into the 4.010 entry bore (pilot clearance 0.040 to 0.060)
alignment.justification: Presented-pose window +-0.70 mm lateral against the +-0.6 mm two-unit PA12 SLS stack. On a 45 deg chamfer an axial push gives a centring force (1 - mu)/(1 + mu) of it, 0.11 at the dry steel-steel upper bound 0.8 (Engineering ToolBox): no wedging while mu < 1. Reference planes: the head flange front face is the head Hirth pitch plane (crest +0.2, root -0.2); both inner lands are recessed 0.25 and never touch; the chamfer runs 0.4 from the land. Sequence: when the lug fronts reach the head's tooth crest plane, the pilot's cylindrical part (from 6.2) is 0.90 past the head pitch plane, 0.25 past the start of the bore cylinder (0.65), so the lugs meet their slots with at most 0.060 mm of lateral error, inside their +-0.6 mm V lead-ins. The pilot then bounds yaw to 0.69 deg; the Hirth teeth centre the seat.

alignment.description: Roll, pitch and yaw: round dia 3 lugs entering 0.6 x 45 deg V lead-ins of the flange and housing slots and the sleeve notches; final roll, centring and pitch by the 36-tooth PTFE-coated Hirth faces
alignment.justification: Roll window +-5.5 deg at the lug tip radius 6.2 against about +-1.4 deg between two units on one table. Before the teeth meet, the lugs index roll within the slot lash, 3.17 to 3.46 deg at the contact radius 3.5, less than half a tooth pitch (5 deg), so the teeth always meet their own gaps. The teeth then roll the tail unit flat (guaranteed draw 1.76 N against 1.39 N needed through PTFE-coated flanks) and pitch it flat (0.21 N needed); pitch on one table is within +-0.73 deg. Yaw stays within the pilot's 0.69 deg, which the lock stage absorbs. Joint angles do not enter: the head unit's head segment and the tail unit's tail segment are each rigid. The open stop puts the sleeve notches over the slots within about +-0.3 deg, inside the +-7.1 deg the V lead-in allows.

alignment.description: Axial closing and seating: the 20 deg capture stage draws the stud 1.0 mm, then the 3 deg lock stage seats the Hirth faces
alignment.justification: Closing force is the coupler motor's: at the 1.5 V closing stall the sleeve gives 14.5 to 16.1 mN m typical (3.6 mN m at the guaranteed lower bound), while drawing one free unit at the mu = 1 table bound needs 1.21 mN m through the capture stage. The axial push that brings the lugs to the capture stage (2.40 mm stroke, about mu W = 0.31 N plus chamfer friction) is not supplied by the candidate: it comes from the experiment's documented start configuration (Q31 item 1) or a later approach design. Tolerance and the yaw residual are taken by sleeve travel to a stall inside the lock stage. No capture window is claimed (CPL-006).

limitations: Approach locomotion is not designed. The coupler engages from a presented pose (stud nose at the bore mouth within +-0.70 mm lateral, +-5.5 deg roll, yaw within the pilot's acceptance) with an external axial push of 2.40 mm. Q31 starts the chain engaged. No capture window is claimed (CPL-006).

Retention is a friction wedge: self-locking needs flank mu > 0.0524 (0.072 at the inner end of the flank line). The cited lower bounds give 2.86x dry and 1.91x oiled at the mean radius, but self-locking is not absolute under vibration or shock (Wikipedia Leadscrew); the bending chain's vibration level is not known. Walking by torsion slip is excluded by the Hirth teeth; walking by vibration is not analysed (Gate 2/3). The cited friction rows are for steel on bronze; C95400 aluminium bronze is taken as a bronze.

The bonded PTFE film on the head teeth must stay off the cam flank: PTFE on the flank would lower the flank friction toward 0.05, below the self-locking condition. The film is bonded to the tooth flanks only.

Preload is typical 6.62 to 13.50 N; the guaranteed lower bound from the datasheet is 1.76 N. At that bound the faces may gap by micrometres under the declared bending (retention and tooth engagement do not depend on it). There is no engagement or current sensor; the controller measures the cell voltage and drives for a fixed time, so it cannot confirm the engaged state (Q32).
Release needs the cell at 3.75 V or more; below that the joint stays locked until recharged (bounded release still holds at that state of charge).

Friction values are handbook values, not tests of these pairs: flank steel on bronze (Wikipedia Leadscrew, raw wikitext), PTFE on steel, steel on steel and nylon on steel (Engineering ToolBox, raw HTML). Mesh efficiency 0.9 to 1.0, bronze Poisson ratio 0.33, the 20 kN/mm loop-stiffness lower bound and the PA12 Poisson ratio 0.4 are provisional. LOCTITE 638 strengths are for steel pins and collars; the gearhead housing material is not stated in the motor datasheet.

Declared loads are modelling assumptions: tension 4 mu W with mu = 1, torsion 2 W x 12.7 mm, out-of-plane bending W x 48.0 mm (site-to-site pitch), in-plane bending equal to the joint drive limit. Joint stall at 3.6 V (fault) gives 52.2 mN m; the lug contact then reaches Hertz 283 MPa, still below the C95400 onset.

The joint motor torque is limited by PWM to the rated 3 mN m (14.5 mN m at the joint). Holding a curvature unpowered is not claimed (Q31 item 6). Pushing two units sideways at a table mu of 1 would need about 30 mN m: Q31 bending adequacy is unresolved.
There is no joint angle sensor. Joint position control is unresolved.

All screw joints to PA12 put the thread in 304 (nut blocks, the stud flange, hinge legs, the lower plate and the motor clip); PA12 sees bearing only, compared with the Materialise PA12 tensile strength 48 MPa (no compressive or bearing strength is cited). Thread engagements are short (0.6 to 0.8 mm); the loads are a few newtons against a stripping capacity of several hundred. The tail stud screws are driven from inside through the open top with a short L key before the controller is fitted (countersunk hex-socket micro screws; the exact screw form is not a standard ISO size and is provisional).

The Hirth rings are small (36 teeth, about 0.39 mm high, r 2.6 to 6.3; the head ring loses 35 percent to the lug slots) and need fine machining (for example wire EDM); the 0.05 mm flank contact band used for their pressure is provisional. 304 teeth and the 304 pilot in the 304 bore can gall.

Gear and pinion boxes are bounded at their pitch circles toward their mating gear; shafts and the hinge pin inside bores are boxed with the bore part; the housing tube and its front flange are one part declared as two boxes; the motor clip band lies inside the enlarged motor box, and the clip and bond masses are lumped boxes. Shell walls are slabs (one SLS part per segment, separate lids); fasteners and harness are lumped boxes.
The stowed diameter margin is reported by the evaluator. PA12 SLS +-0.3 mm on outer dimensions uses up to about 0.6 mm of it.
Mating roll is 0 deg only (the coupler axis is off the body centre, so a 180 deg roll would stand the unit upside down).
BLE only, no inter-unit data or power path through the coupler.
